compare_blocks.body:
The premise is aligned conditions: the same launch, the same six weeks remaining, the same twenty units, the same level of channel commitment to the date, and creator bookings still negotiable. compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a strategy meeting, someone might notice a pattern in the evidence or ask what a decision will mean a year from now. Either type can raise both questions. Those contributions do not reveal which type someone is. The resemblance comes from the shared N and J — sourcing that looks at patterns and possibility, and an outward habit of forming arrangements and conclusions. That describes two points of emphasis; it does not mean both neglect next month's schedule, and does not say who is more decisive.

The difference sits on E/I and T/F. E/I decides whether attention and energy go outward or inward more often: ENTJ more often pushes things forward in exchanges with people, tasks and occasions; INFJ more often sorts ideas and feelings internally before going outward. T/F decides which kind of basis judgement leans on: ENTJ more often requires criteria that are impersonal and consistently applicable; INFJ more often brings the people involved and their values into the judgement.

The two cannot substitute for each other. Whether someone talks about meaning is not evidence about E/I, and whether a reason is well expressed does not mark the T/F boundary; someone whose delivery is scattered may simply not have organised the language yet.

### The same "we cannot ship now": what each presses for

In a fictional launch review, both reviewers have the same six-week deadline, inventory report and release criteria. One question is whether either date meets the same criteria for staffing and product readiness. Another is what each date would mean for the users and partners who are relying on the launch. Both reviewers can raise both questions before deciding.

Both questions call for evidence, such as what the team has promised users and which features it can verify before release. The counterexamples hold too: ENTJ may argue to ship on time and fix the experience in the next version, and INFJ may ship on time because the contract says so. Role rewrites the wording as well — whoever signs outward commitments usually raises dates more often than whoever owns the content. One conclusion settles nothing.

### Why Ni and Se are shared while the judging pair swaps entirely

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se. The shared names are Ni and Se, in different positions: ENTJ has Ni second and Se third; INFJ has Ni first and Se fourth. On the judging side, ENTJ's Te–Fi and INFJ's Fe–Ti swap as whole pairs.

These positions describe emphasis inside the model. The ENTJ side organises resources and checkable goals outward through Te, with Fi in the fourth position; the INFJ side gathers direction through Ni, with Fe second attending to the people present and shared expectations, and Ti third running a consistency check. Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not consistent across tables, and some give only the function name; when a version differs, check its source, then read the first two positions for this pair — the disagreement does not change the first two.

compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Scope note: the three passages below are editorial composites that describe only how the two communicate and organise information, not handling procedures. Anything involving a property contract, title registration, a mortgage or tax follows local law and professional guidance from a lawyer or bank; anything involving product safety or industry compliance follows the regulator and professional advice. Where a situation is unclear, seek help first and then act on that guidance.

Working together on a launch, one more often watches "when we must ship" and the other "whether we are actually ready when we ship". Both are needed, and friction usually appears when the date and the basis do not line up.

### Setting the rhythm for a product launch

(Fictional scene.) Six weeks to launch, only twenty units have arrived, creator bookings must be locked four weeks ahead, and the channel has promised a date verbally without signing. One approach works backwards from resources: how the twenty units split across core channels, how much of the gap a booking-based trial can cover, and what has to be renegotiated if the channel date moves. The other confirms whether the missing build would change what users can actually do with the product. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

Both lines have to land on the same sheet, and two cases can be handled separately. If only the communication material is not ready — copy, assets, demo script — keep the public purchase date and set a clear content review date, changing no public commitment before it. If the core feature does not meet the agreed release criteria, move the date; or, after stating the scope and the limits honestly, open a limited trial and write the unavailable features into the public description.

The costs sit on either side. Shipping on time holds the window, but the first reviews set the shape; moving the date protects the experience, but channel and creator schedules must be renegotiated, and the cost lands on relationships and time. Which is better depends on where the acceptance line is drawn, what the contract says about penalties, and how much capacity the team really has — not on type.

A checklist helps: split the launch items into two columns, "must hold before we ship" and "better if it holds", and give every item a checkable condition and an owner. Anything without a condition is recorded as insufficient information and the facts are gathered; anything in the second column that nobody objected to needs checking whether it has no owner or is genuinely unimportant, rather than being assumed unimportant.

### The follow-up: whether to delay for a principle

(Fictional scene.) This continues the previous discussion, same launch and same people, with the meeting moving from scheduling to "should we move the date". The side arguing to ship usually lays out the cost of delay as checkable items: channel slots, the competitor window, two weeks of team capacity; and asks the other side to say what a delay buys back. The side arguing to delay usually states first what has to be protected: which gap would be remembered in the version shipped on time, and how long it would take to repair afterwards.

The disagreement is usually not about who cares more about the product, but about which basis each cites. A workable move is to put both sentences into checkable form: ask the delay side to write "which signals appearing would show that shipping on time really did damage the experience"; ask the ship side to write "which single condition failing would move the date immediately". With both written, the meeting has a shared basis.

Being unable to produce a metric does not mean there is no basis, and does not mean avoidance. It may be insufficient information (no data on user response yet), different standards (one looks at first reviews, the other at long-term reputation), or simply something not easy to say in the room. Work out which, then decide what information to gather and where to hold the conversation.

### Two friends buying a small flat together

(Fictional scene.) Two friends who have known each other for ten years want to buy a small two-bedroom flat together, each paying half the deposit. One approach starts from executable terms: ownership shares, who lives there, how the mortgage is split, and what happens if one wants to sell in a few years. The other tests whether the relationship can bear those terms: how to raise it if one of them marries and needs the flat, and whether talking about money will damage a ten-year friendship. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

Both preparations have a cost. The one who sets terms first may make the other feel "you already planned the exit"; the one who talks about the relationship first may postpone what should be written down until prices and rates have moved. The difference is closer to where Te and Fe put their effort — one turns shared property into executable terms, the other first checks whether the relationship can hold those terms — but either order can work. Keep the counterexamples: at this amount, INFJ may also demand the terms be written first; when the other person is clearly uneasy, ENTJ may also leave the numbers alone for now.

The friends can bring their questions about ownership, financing and exit terms to qualified local advisers. The example focuses on the conversation. An exercise: each writes one line, "how I would want to exit in the worst case", without debating right and wrong, read them aloud, then each explains the concern behind the line. If someone changes the wording while reading, ask whether they changed the term or the concern, rather than deciding they have not thought it through.

A direct comment can sound uncompromising, but either person can be direct. To discuss T/F, ask whether the judgement emphasises consistent criteria or the values and circumstances of the people affected. Tone alone does not tell you which criteria someone considered.

The second is assigning "talks about meaning" to F and treating it as evidence-free. In the convention used here, ENTJ’s Fi is fourth and INFJ’s Ti is third. These positions do not establish how either person expresses a value or checks an argument. Conversely, F wants evidence too, only it more often asks first what the matter means for the people involved.

The fifth is inferring from the shared N and J that neither cares about near-term scheduling. Attention to scheduling depends far more on the role, the duty and the risk being carried at the time.

(Fictional scene.) Six weeks to launch, only twenty units have arrived, creator bookings must be locked four weeks ahead, and the channel has promised a date verbally without signing. One approach works backwards from resources: how the twenty units split across core channels, how much of the gap a booking-based trial can cover, and what has to be renegotiated if the channel date moves. The other confirms whether the missing build would change what users can actually do with the product. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

Both lines have to land on the same sheet, and two cases can be handled separately. If only the communication material is not ready — copy, assets, demo script — keep the public purchase date and set a clear content review date, changing no public commitment before it. body: In a strategy meeting, someone might notice a pattern in the evidence or ask what a decision will mean a year from now. Either type can raise both questions. Those contributions do not reveal which type someone is. The resemblance comes from the shared N and J — sourcing that looks at patterns and possibility, and an outward habit of forming arrangements and conclusions. That describes two points of emphasis; it does not mean both neglect next month's schedule, and does not say who is more decisive.

The difference sits on E/I and T/F. E/I decides whether attention and energy go outward or inward more often: ENTJ more often pushes things forward in exchanges with people, tasks and occasions; INFJ more often sorts ideas and feelings internally before going outward. T/F decides which kind of basis judgement leans on: ENTJ more often requires criteria that are impersonal and consistently applicable; INFJ more often brings the people involved and their values into the judgement.

The two cannot substitute for each other. Whether someone talks about meaning is not evidence about E/I, and whether a reason is well expressed does not mark the T/F boundary; someone whose delivery is scattered may simply not have organised the language yet.
### The same "we cannot ship now": what each presses for

In a fictional launch review, both reviewers have the same six-week deadline, inventory report and release criteria. One question is whether either date meets the same criteria for staffing and product readiness. Another is what each date would mean for the users and partners who are relying on the launch. Both reviewers can raise both questions before deciding.

Both questions call for evidence, such as what the team has promised users and which features it can verify before release. The counterexamples hold too: ENTJ may argue to ship on time and fix the experience in the next version, and INFJ may ship on time because the contract says so. Role rewrites the wording as well — whoever signs outward commitments usually raises dates more often than whoever owns the content. One conclusion settles nothing.
### Why Ni and Se are shared while the judging pair swaps entirely

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se. The shared names are Ni and Se, in different positions: ENTJ has Ni second and Se third; INFJ has Ni first and Se fourth. On the judging side, ENTJ's Te–Fi and INFJ's Fe–Ti swap as whole pairs.

These positions describe emphasis inside the model. The ENTJ side organises resources and checkable goals outward through Te, with Fi in the fourth position; the INFJ side gathers direction through Ni, with Fe second attending to the people present and shared expectations, and Ti third running a consistency check. Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not consistent across tables, and some give only the function name; when a version differs, check its source, then read the first two positions for this pair — the disagreement does not change the first two.

A position is not a step, and cannot be used to derive who speaks first, who is better at the numbers, or whose values are firmer, still less whether two people work well together. Both base pages are the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and the [INFJ profile](/en/personality/infj).

body: Scope note: the three passages below are editorial composites that describe only how the two communicate and organise information, not handling procedures. Anything involving a property contract, title registration, a mortgage or tax follows local law and professional guidance from a lawyer or bank; anything involving product safety or industry compliance follows the regulator and professional advice. Where a situation is unclear, seek help first and then act on that guidance.

### Setting the rhythm for a product launch

(Fictional scene.) Six weeks to launch, only twenty units have arrived, creator bookings must be locked four weeks ahead, and the channel has promised a date verbally without signing. One approach works backwards from resources: how the twenty units split across core channels, how much of the gap a booking-based trial can cover, and what has to be renegotiated if the channel date moves. The other confirms whether the missing build would change what users can actually do with the product. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

Both lines have to land on the same sheet, and two cases can be handled separately. If only the communication material is not ready — copy, assets, demo script — keep the public purchase date and set a clear content review date, changing no public commitment before it. If the core feature does not meet the agreed release criteria, move the date; or, after stating the scope and the limits honestly, open a limited trial and write the unavailable features into the public description.

The costs sit on either side. Shipping on time holds the window, but the first reviews set the shape; moving the date protects the experience, but channel and creator schedules must be renegotiated, and the cost lands on relationships and time. Anything without a condition is recorded as insufficient information and the facts are gathered; anything in the second column that nobody objected to needs checking whether it has no owner or is genuinely unimportant, rather than being assumed unimportant.

(Fictional scene.) This continues the previous discussion, same launch and same people, with the meeting moving from scheduling to "should we move the date". The side arguing to delay usually states first what has to be protected: which gap would be remembered in the version shipped on time, and how long it would take to repair afterwards.

It may be insufficient information (no data on user response yet), different standards (one looks at first reviews, the other at long-term reputation), or simply something not easy to say in the room. comparison_public_projection_v1.summary:
ENTJ and INFJ share N and J and differ on E/I and T/F. Each difference has its own meaning and cannot be flattened into "one is more rational, one is more about meaning".

- E/I: the ENTJ side, E, turns attention and energy more toward tasks, people and occasions outside; the INFJ side, I, turns more toward inner ideas and feelings. This describes direction, not social skill and not how much someone talks; both may speak a lot in a meeting and both need quiet afterwards.
- T/F: the ENTJ side, T, more often judges by impersonal criteria that can be applied consistently; the INFJ side, F, more often puts people, relationships and values into the judgement. Both sides want evidence; the difference is which basis is taken first more often.
- Shared N (Intuition): both more often take connections, patterns and likely directions rather than stopping at each fact. Shared J (Judging): facing the outer world, both more often form arrangements and conclusions first. Sharing these two letters does not mean both pay the same attention to next month's schedule or to on-site detail — that depends far more on duty and experience.

Using the type-dynamics convention on this page, the stacks are: Te–Ni–Se–Fi for ENTJ and Ni–Fe–Ti–Se for INFJ. The two share Ni and Se in different positions; on the judging side, Te–Fi becomes Fe–Ti. The attitude of the third process (Se for ENTJ, Ti for INFJ) is disputed elsewhere, and this writing is a convention adopted here, not the Foundation's only version. Positions describe emphasis in preference, not the order of behaviour, the division of work, or whether a collaboration runs smoothly.

In the same launch, either may argue for the date or for moving it; what can be compared is which kind of evidence each more often presses for.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
In a strategy meeting, someone might notice a pattern in the evidence or ask what a decision will mean a year from now. Either type can raise both questions. Those contributions do not reveal which type someone is. The resemblance comes from the shared N and J — sourcing that looks at patterns and possibility, and an outward habit of forming arrangements and conclusions. That describes two points of emphasis; it does not mean both neglect next month's schedule, and does not say who is more decisive.

The difference sits on E/I and T/F. E/I decides whether attention and energy go outward or inward more often: ENTJ more often pushes things forward in exchanges with people, tasks and occasions; INFJ more often sorts ideas and feelings internally before going outward. T/F decides which kind of basis judgement leans on: ENTJ more often requires criteria that are impersonal and consistently applicable; INFJ more often brings the people involved and their values into the judgement.

The two cannot substitute for each other. Whether someone talks about meaning is not evidence about E/I, and whether a reason is well expressed does not mark the T/F boundary; someone whose delivery is scattered may simply not have organised the language yet.

### The same "we cannot ship now": what each presses for

In a fictional launch review, both reviewers have the same six-week deadline, inventory report and release criteria. One question is whether either date meets the same criteria for staffing and product readiness. Another is what each date would mean for the users and partners who are relying on the launch. Both reviewers can raise both questions before deciding.

Both questions call for evidence, such as what the team has promised users and which features it can verify before release. The counterexamples hold too: ENTJ may argue to ship on time and fix the experience in the next version, and INFJ may ship on time because the contract says so. Role rewrites the wording as well — whoever signs outward commitments usually raises dates more often than whoever owns the content. One conclusion settles nothing.

### Why Ni and Se are shared while the judging pair swaps entirely

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se. The shared names are Ni and Se, in different positions: ENTJ has Ni second and Se third; INFJ has Ni first and Se fourth. On the judging side, ENTJ's Te–Fi and INFJ's Fe–Ti swap as whole pairs.

These positions describe emphasis inside the model. The ENTJ side organises resources and checkable goals outward through Te, with Fi in the fourth position; the INFJ side gathers direction through Ni, with Fe second attending to the people present and shared expectations, and Ti third running a consistency check. Whether the third process is labelled introverted or extraverted is not consistent across tables, and some give only the function name; when a version differs, check its source, then read the first two positions for this pair — the disagreement does not change the first two.

A position is not a step, and cannot be used to derive who speaks first, who is better at the numbers, or whose values are firmer, still less whether two people work well together. Both base pages are the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and the [INFJ profile](/en/personality/infj).

sections.body_md:
The premise is aligned conditions: the same launch, the same six weeks remaining, the same twenty units, the same level of channel commitment to the date, and creator bookings still negotiable. If one signs outward contracts and the other only owns the content, their different responsibilities can explain what they focus on.

One launch, one group of people, one go-live date; the six rows fall on different axes and the last column names which one. On any row either type can take the other's approach; the table records only which is taken first more often.

| The same event (six weeks, twenty units, the same channel commitment) | ENTJ: the basis more likely attended to | INFJ: the basis more likely attended to | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The core feature is one build short; the date can move | Apply the same release criteria to both dates using the confirmed build and staffing estimates | Weigh how each of the same dates would affect users, partners and existing commitments | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| Who fronts the launch publicly | Who holds the data and the decision rights, and who can answer questions live | Who would be most believed on this segment, and how the room would receive it | Launch roles; either type still checks decision rights, information and audience needs |
| Both consider which creator to book four weeks ahead | Evaluate the confirmed cost and cancellation terms of each option against the same criteria | Weigh how the same options would come across to the intended audience and partners | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| Whether to add an internal rehearsal three days out | May clarify the rehearsal’s purpose by discussing the same proposal with the team | May clarify the proposal’s purpose by reflecting on it privately | E/I: where attention goes while making sense of the same proposal. Both can use either approach. |
| Which table the review opens with | Goal attainment, and how much of the channel commitment was met | Whether the first sentence was heard as what we meant to say | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| Whether this still holds in a year | Whether the goal and the resource structure still stand up | Whether the original judgement still holds | Shared N and J; does not separate the two |

The differences in the table are not a scale of ability. An INFJ who has coordinated launches for years more often asks about acceptance items first; an ENTJ running a launch for the first time may care only about the narrative. The same person also acts differently with different authority, information and people present, so these rows cannot be used to classify.
sections.title: ENTJ and INFJ in one minute

sections.body_md:
Scope note: the three passages below are editorial composites that describe only how the two communicate and organise information, not handling procedures. Anything involving a property contract, title registration, a mortgage or tax follows local law and professional guidance from a lawyer or bank; anything involving product safety or industry compliance follows the regulator and professional advice. Where a situation is unclear, seek help first and then act on that guidance.

Working together on a launch, one more often watches "when we must ship" and the other "whether we are actually ready when we ship". Both are needed, and friction usually appears when the date and the basis do not line up.

### Setting the rhythm for a product launch

(Fictional scene.) Six weeks to launch, only twenty units have arrived, creator bookings must be locked four weeks ahead, and the channel has promised a date verbally without signing. One approach works backwards from resources: how the twenty units split across core channels, how much of the gap a booking-based trial can cover, and what has to be renegotiated if the channel date moves. The other confirms whether the missing build would change what users can actually do with the product. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

Both lines have to land on the same sheet, and two cases can be handled separately. If only the communication material is not ready — copy, assets, demo script — keep the public purchase date and set a clear content review date, changing no public commitment before it. If the core feature does not meet the agreed release criteria, move the date; or, after stating the scope and the limits honestly, open a limited trial and write the unavailable features into the public description.

The costs sit on either side. Shipping on time holds the window, but the first reviews set the shape; moving the date protects the experience, but channel and creator schedules must be renegotiated, and the cost lands on relationships and time. Which is better depends on where the acceptance line is drawn, what the contract says about penalties, and how much capacity the team really has — not on type.

A checklist helps: split the launch items into two columns, "must hold before we ship" and "better if it holds", and give every item a checkable condition and an owner. Anything without a condition is recorded as insufficient information and the facts are gathered; anything in the second column that nobody objected to needs checking whether it has no owner or is genuinely unimportant, rather than being assumed unimportant.

### The follow-up: whether to delay for a principle

(Fictional scene.) This continues the previous discussion, same launch and same people, with the meeting moving from scheduling to "should we move the date". The side arguing to ship usually lays out the cost of delay as checkable items: channel slots, the competitor window, two weeks of team capacity; and asks the other side to say what a delay buys back. The side arguing to delay usually states first what has to be protected: which gap would be remembered in the version shipped on time, and how long it would take to repair afterwards.

The disagreement is usually not about who cares more about the product, but about which basis each cites. A workable move is to put both sentences into checkable form: ask the delay side to write "which signals appearing would show that shipping on time really did damage the experience"; ask the ship side to write "which single condition failing would move the date immediately". With both written, the meeting has a shared basis.

Being unable to produce a metric does not mean there is no basis, and does not mean avoidance. It may be insufficient information (no data on user response yet), different standards (one looks at first reviews, the other at long-term reputation), or simply something not easy to say in the room. Work out which, then decide what information to gather and where to hold the conversation.

### Two friends buying a small flat together

(Fictional scene.) Two friends who have known each other for ten years want to buy a small two-bedroom flat together, each paying half the deposit. One approach starts from executable terms: ownership shares, who lives there, how the mortgage is split, and what happens if one wants to sell in a few years. The other tests whether the relationship can bear those terms: how to raise it if one of them marries and needs the flat, and whether talking about money will damage a ten-year friendship. Either approach can be used by the same person, and the order depends on the task and the information available.

Both preparations have a cost. The one who sets terms first may make the other feel "you already planned the exit"; the one who talks about the relationship first may postpone what should be written down until prices and rates have moved. The difference is closer to where Te and Fe put their effort — one turns shared property into executable terms, the other first checks whether the relationship can hold those terms — but either order can work. Keep the counterexamples: at this amount, INFJ may also demand the terms be written first; when the other person is clearly uneasy, ENTJ may also leave the numbers alone for now.

The friends can bring their questions about ownership, financing and exit terms to qualified local advisers. The example focuses on the conversation. An exercise: each writes one line, "how I would want to exit in the worst case", without debating right and wrong, read them aloud, then each explains the concern behind the line. If someone changes the wording while reading, ask whether they changed the term or the concern, rather than deciding they have not thought it through.

sections.body_md:
A direct comment can sound uncompromising, but either person can be direct. To discuss T/F, ask whether the judgement emphasises consistent criteria or the values and circumstances of the people affected. Tone alone does not tell you which criteria someone considered.

The second is assigning "talks about meaning" to F and treating it as evidence-free. In the convention used here, ENTJ’s Fi is fourth and INFJ’s Ti is third. These positions do not establish how either person expresses a value or checks an argument. Conversely, F wants evidence too, only it more often asks first what the matter means for the people involved.

The third is treating a delay as indecision. A delay may raise the acceptance standard, or protect the meaning already promised publicly; both are judgements. Shipping on time is not proof of decisiveness either.

The fourth is treating E as sociable and I as afraid of communication. E/I describes which side attention and energy go to more often: ENTJ also needs time alone after a meeting, and INFJ can organise a roomful of people when it is needed.

The fifth is inferring from the shared N and J that neither cares about near-term scheduling. Attention to scheduling depends far more on the role, the duty and the risk being carried at the time.
sections.title: ENTJ and INFJ: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
When earlier and later results differ, check the item bank, language version, scoring convention and what you were referring to: a project at work, or a relationship in life. A role with business targets or responsibility for others’ wellbeing can affect which situations you picture when answering. Record the role and the choices you were actually free to make before interpreting a change in results.

Make the practice a non-scored review. Pick a few recent launch or collaboration decisions and write three lines for each: what information you had and what was missing; which standard you used to judge whether the date should move, and which part was checkable and which relied on reading people; who was affected, and what your role and authority allowed you to do. Then add one separate line: in this matter, did attention sit more on what was happening outside, or on sorting it out internally, and which kind of exchange drained you more over the day.

The notes are for reflection only, are not scored, and do not assign a type. Whether someone can turn expression into conditions on the spot, what roles they prefer and the order of their actions cannot be used to judge type; using the other kind of basis on the same matter shows both approaches are within range, not that the type changed.

items.answer:
Not speed. The two share N and J and differ on E/I and T/F: whether attention and energy go outward or inward more often, and whether judgement rests on impersonal consistent criteria or on people and values.

In the same launch, ENTJ more often asks "what acceptance items does a delay buy back", and INFJ more often asks "which public commitments break and how are user expectations managed". Either may argue to ship and either to delay; who speaks faster is not a criterion.
items.question: Is the disagreement about speed or about standards?

items.answer:
In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INFJ is Ni–Fe–Ti–Se: the shared Ni and Se sit in different positions, and the judging side swaps Te–Fi for Fe–Ti as whole pairs.

Sharing Ni means both more often look at patterns and possibility first; it does not mean they use the same ruler. Positions describe emphasis only, do not predict who does what first, and do not say who is better at coordination. The labelling of the third process is disputed elsewhere, so check the source when a writing differs.
items.question: They share two function processes, so why is the judging so far apart?

items.answer:
Yes. T/F describes which kind of basis is taken first more often, not whether the other capacity exists.

Under this writing INFJ's Ti sits third, and a consistency check will equally pursue whether a standard can be applied uniformly; ENTJ's Fi is fourth in this convention, but that position does not tell you whether someone will explain their values aloud. What discriminates better is which kind of reason is cited first across comparable situations, not one contribution in a meeting.
items.question: INFJ also uses objective standards, and ENTJ also talks about values?

items.answer:
Both types can do it; competence depends on experience, authority and delivery requirements, not on type.

Launch coordination includes setting the rhythm, locking resources, preparing content, controlling risk and reviewing. Take the same fictional launch sheet and write one version as "a six-week backwards plan with acceptance items", the other as "the one sentence the launch must say plus a list of public commitments", and see which you would rather do repeatedly, then compare with the duties of a real role and your delivery record. Which comes more easily reflects experience and interest.
items.question: Who is better suited to coordinating a product launch?

items.answer:
Two possible sources of friction are changing a date people thought was final and asking for a decision before someone has had time to think it through.

A workable agreement is to record the two kinds of information separately: confirmed acceptance items, and concerns not yet verified, each in its own column, with a shared review time to look at both. In an argument, ask first "if this proves false, what do we change; if it proves true, what do we change", so both people can compare conditions and consequences.
items.question: Where do ENTJ and INFJ most often get stuck on a launch?

items.answer:
Check the assessment name, version, language and scoring convention first, then whether you were referring to a project at work or a relationship in life when you answered.

If the item bank reports dimension scores, look at whether E/I or T/F sits closer to the boundary; read it by that tool's own scoring notes, since sitting near a boundary only means that label is sensitive to changes in your answers, not that two types both hold, and not that you can switch freely between two ways of deciding. Without dimension scores or scoring notes, do not infer a boundary, and no retest interval is prescribed.
